newsitem.title: UK: Unichem, Gehe deadlocked on British chemists Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Unichem, Gehe deadlocked on British chemists Lloyds.

text.p: A long-running battle between Britain's Unichem Plc and Germany's Gehe AG to buy pharmacy chain operator Lloyds Chemists Plc was deadlocked on Monday as this month's deadline for the rival bids neared.
Unichem said it held 10.1 percent of Lloyds, including acceptances representing about 0.4 percent of the target's ordinary shares -- barely changed from the level it reported a month ago.
Gehe responded by downplaying its rival's statement.

"Unichem already said that it had around this level of acceptances and this announcement is a pure formality, a question of a few digits behind the decimal point. It shows that acceptances on both sides are still very low," a Gehe spokesman said in Germany.
Gehe said on December 23 that it had received valid acceptances of its offer representing about 0.16 percent of Lloyds' ordinary shares.
Both companies have until January 17 to raise their offers and the Gehe spokesman said his company would continue to wait.
For its part, Lloyds, which had yet to take action on either offer, said it continued to advise investors to wait and see whether the firms raise their bids.

"It's our intention to announce our second-half sales figures either tomorrow or the day after," a Lloyds spokesman said, adding that the company normally released the results in the first 10 days of the year.
The spokesman said Lloyds was not expecting to make any further statements on the bid situation ahead of January 17.
At the end of last week, Unichem's stock and cash offer valued Lloyds at about 486 pence per share, while Gehe's all-cash bid stood at 500 pence, the Lloyds spokesman said.
The value of Unichem's offer has fallen with the company's share price in recent weeks.
Lloyds' shares rose 4.5 pence to 514.5 by 1350 GMT, while Unichem gained 0.5 pence to 246.5 pence.
In Frankfurt, Gehe's shares rose 30 pfennigs to 97.90 marks.
